svg.aria-label: SonarQube-Lens — Multi-Agent AI Code-Quality Analysis and Remediation for a SonarQube finding. A finding from any project — a BUG, VULNERABILITY, CODE_SMELL or SECURITY_HOTSPOT at any severity from BLOCKER to INFO — is pasted as a URL or issue key, or delivered by a Quality-Gate webhook, and analysed by ten agents in four phases. Phase one, COLLECT: SonarFetcher pulls the issue and rule facts from the SonarQube API; CodeFetcher re-reads the real source at the analysed commit through a multi-provider grounding chain; GitForensics finds who introduced it, when, and in which pull request. Phase two, ADJUDICATE: the PerspectiveAnalyst runs six independent perspectives — rule intent, code context, runtime risk, repo norms, history and ownership, and security and compliance — each returning a typed sub-verdict with a quoted line; the FalsePositiveJudge computes a deterministic 0 to 100 percent false-positive probability and emits one verdict — MUST FIX, ACCEPTABLE RISK, NEEDS DISCUSSION or FALSE POSITIVE. Phase three, PRESCRIBE: the FixSpecifier ranks concrete fixes from minimal change to refactor to redesign, self-reviewed; the Reviewer runs two independent rubrics in two LLM calls, Diagnosis sixty plus Fix forty, and can send the work back with REVISE in a bounded loop. Phase four, ACT and NOTIFY: the Jira Agent raises a deduplicated SIR, the Remediator marks a false positive or opens a fix pull request only on APPROVE plus a human gate and dry-run by default, and the Notifier always reports to Microsoft Teams and email. The Orchestrator coordinates all four phases and an orchestration crash never changes your build; the deterministic core always runs and the LLM layer enriches it when a key is present.
svg.title: SonarQube-Lens — ten agents, four phases (Collect · Adjudicate · Prescribe · Act and Notify), one verdict — for a SonarQube finding
